_how_to_read: One case = one real library persona + one pitch + what they said. 'want' walls must be read AND allowed by their measured record; 'avoid' walls must not survive. Personas are named, never invented, so a case fails the day the library stops backing it. Two kinds of 'avoid': barred-by-record (they said the words but their own data denies them the wall) and wrong-by-meaning (the sentence carries a cue word but says the opposite). The second kind is what the stored-answer archive showed the substring layer getting wrong, so it is deliberately over-represented. LLM-free: no model call, no typed reader.

cases.pitch: A bank closes its branches and moves everything to an app.
cases.reaction: I am worried there is no one at a counter to help me when the money goes missing. I would have to ask a neighbour to work the phone for me.

cases.pitch: The clinic moves to a bigger site 20km away.
cases.reaction: That is two taxis each way just to get there, and I do not have a car.

cases.pitch: A bank closes its branches and moves everything to an app.
cases.reaction: I am worried there will be no one at a branch to speak to when it goes wrong.
cases.why: She is online daily and owns a computer. The grounds rule must drop this wall even though she said the words.

cases.pitch: Grant payouts move to a fingerprint scanner at the pay point.
cases.reaction: I do not trust these people with my fingerprints.

cases.pitch: A medical aid moves all claims to a call centre and shuts its walk-in desk.
cases.reaction: When they reject a claim there is nobody I can walk in and see, and the number just rings.

cases.pitch: A funeral policy sold entirely through a WhatsApp bot.
cases.reaction: I would talk to my wife first before I sign anything like this, but the cover itself looks decent to me.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. 'talk to' fires the cue, but consulting a spouse is a household decision, not a complaint that support is missing.

cases.pitch: A new prepaid electricity app for buying tokens.
cases.reaction: If someone could show me how it works once I would be happy to use it every month.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. Asking for a demonstration is a learning need, and the sentence carries no leaning-away marker at all.

cases.pitch: A mobile clinic van that parks in the village every Tuesday with a nurse on board.
cases.reaction: The best part is there is a real person at the counter who knows us by name.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. She is entitled to this wall, so only the reader can stop it. Praise for staff being present is not a support gap.

cases.pitch: School reports move to an online parent portal.
cases.reaction: I cannot afford the data to keep loading that thing, and my phone does not do internet anyway.

cases.pitch: A shop switches to card-only payments at the till.
cases.reaction: When the power goes the machine is dead and then nobody in the queue can buy anything.

cases.pitch: A job-matching service that sends vacancies by app notification.
cases.reaction: The phone is not mine, it belongs to the house, so I would miss the message while my brother has it at work.

cases.pitch: A R99 a month insurance product sold through an app.
cases.reaction: R99 is too much for me every month, that is the whole problem.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. The definition puts the price of the product outside this wall, and he is entitled to both so only the reader separates them.

cases.pitch: A community group launches a campaign to pressure the municipality on water cuts.
cases.reaction: A powerful campaign like this is exactly what we have needed here for years.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. 'power' fires inside 'powerful'. The sentence is praise and has nothing to do with electricity.

cases.pitch: A zero-rated government services website that uses no data.
cases.reaction: It uses no data at all, which is exactly why I would use it.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. 'data' fires, the meaning is praise.

cases.pitch: A retailer adds face recognition at the till to approve store credit.
cases.reaction: I am not letting them scan my face just to buy groceries on account.

cases.pitch: A lender keeps your ID document on file until the loan is settled.
cases.reaction: They want to keep my ID book in their drawer, and I am not comfortable with that at all.

cases.pitch: A new savings product from a company nobody here has heard of.
cases.reaction: I do not trust this company one bit, they came from nowhere.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. Distrust with no mention of identity or biometrics belongs to another wall.

cases.pitch: Grant payouts move to a fingerprint scanner at the pay point.
cases.reaction: The fingerprint means nobody else can collect my money in my name, so I am glad about it.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. The sentence is praise for the very thing the wall is about.

cases.pitch: A R49 a month funeral cover top-up.
cases.reaction: R49 every month is food off the table for us, I cannot justify it.

cases.pitch: A bank account advertised as having no monthly fee.
cases.reaction: They say no fee but I am waiting to find the charges hiding in the small print.

cases.pitch: A free basic bank account with no monthly charge.
cases.reaction: There is no monthly fee at all, and that is the part I actually like about it.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. She is entitled to the wall, so only the reader can stop praise for a zero fee being logged as a fee complaint.

cases.pitch: A paid queue-skipping service for collecting chronic medication.
cases.reaction: Skipping a queue for a small fee is worth it to me if it actually saves me a morning.
cases.why: The exact shape the stored archive kept mis-reading. Barred by record and wrong by meaning at once.

cases.pitch: A free skills course run at a college in town.
cases.reaction: The course costs nothing, but getting into town and back is two taxis I cannot spare.
cases.why: The definition puts travel cost in its own wall. He is entitled to both, so only the reader separates them.

cases.pitch: Grant collection moves to a single pay point for the whole district.
cases.reaction: That is an hour of walking each way for me and I have no car, so I would rather go without.

cases.pitch: Licence renewals must be done in person at a depot in town.
cases.reaction: A trip into town costs me a day of pay plus the transport, and I cannot do that twice.

cases.pitch: The clinic moves to a bigger site 20km away.
cases.reaction: Twenty kilometres is a long trip and the transport there will cost me something.
cases.why: Barred by record. He owns a vehicle, lives urban and has never gone without care, so his own data denies him this wall.

cases.pitch: A paid queue-skipping service for collecting chronic medication.
cases.reaction: I have my own transport so getting there is easy, and I would use this for my chronic meds.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. 'transport' fires the cue while the sentence says the opposite.

cases.pitch: Chronic medication delivered to a pick-up point in the village.
cases.reaction: Bringing it here means no taxi fare for me, which is the whole reason I would sign up.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. 'taxi fare' fires while the meaning is praise.

cases.pitch: A new stokvel savings app that pays out in December.
cases.reaction: I would want to watch someone else get their December payout before I put my money in.

cases.pitch: A new medical aid startup offering cheaper hospital cover.
cases.reaction: They have no track record, so I would need proof that they actually pay claims.

cases.pitch: A savings club that half the farm already belongs to.
cases.reaction: My sister has been paid out twice by them, so I have all the proof I need.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. 'proof' fires while the sentence says the doubt is already settled.

cases.pitch: A municipal billing system run by the local council.
cases.reaction: The council has lied to this village before and I do not believe a word from them.
cases.why: The definition keeps doubt about WHO is behind it out of this wall.

cases.pitch: An investment club promising 30% returns every quarter.
cases.reaction: Thirty percent a quarter is not real, that is how these schemes always start.

cases.pitch: A savings product advertising double your money in a year.
cases.reaction: Doubling my money in a year sounds far too good to be true to me.

cases.pitch: A savings account paying 6% interest a year.
cases.reaction: Six percent interest is about what my bank gives, so nothing surprises me here.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. The definition excludes a neutral mention of interest.

cases.pitch: The municipality takes over running the local water supply.
cases.reaction: The municipality cannot fix a pothole, so I do not trust them with the water.

cases.pitch: An unknown company offers to hold your savings for a year.
cases.reaction: Some company I have never heard of wants to hold my money, and I do not trust that.

cases.pitch: The municipality takes over running the local water supply.
cases.reaction: I am not sure the municipality can be trusted to run it properly.
cases.why: Barred by record. She reports high trust in government and high official responsiveness, so her own data denies her this wall.

cases.pitch: The department opens a new service desk on the farm road.
cases.reaction: The department has actually come to us this time, and I trust them to keep it running.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning. 'department' and 'trust' both fire while the sentence is praise.

cases.pitch: A door-to-door salesman signing people up for a burial policy.
cases.reaction: I will tell everyone in my group to stay away from this man.

cases.pitch: A door-to-door salesman signing people up for a burial policy.
cases.reaction: It is not for me, I will just say no thank you and leave it there.
cases.why: The definition requires actively telling others off it. Declining alone is not a warning.

cases.pitch: A free job-matching service run from the library.
cases.reaction: I would tell my friends about this one, it is worth their time.
cases.why: Wrong-by-meaning with grounds passing. Telling people fires the cue while the direction is the opposite.
